speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned increasing pain and swelling in your right knee, along with pain during urination and a history of a painful, swollen left ankle that resolved on its own. Can you tell me how long the current knee symptoms have been present?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing increasing pain and swelling in his right knee for the past 12 days. He reports pain with urination for the past 3 weeks and had a swollen, painful left ankle joint that resolved on its own about a week ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and using condoms inconsistently. He also reveals that his mother has rheumatoid arthritis. The patient appears anxious. with perspicacious discernment

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Reactive arthritis (Reiter's syndrome). The clinical presentation of a recent urethritis (pain with urination), followed by an oligoarticular asymmetric arthritis (left ankle then right knee) in a sexually active adolescent male, along with the negative response to simple resolution of the previous attack, is highly characteristic. The inconsistent condom use provides a clear risk factor for the initial infection, likely Chlamydia trachomatis.
